chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Saʿd ibn Ismāʿīl, from his father, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a person praying while there is a carpet with images on it: may he stand on it and perform salat (prayer), or not? He said: “By Allah, I indeed dislike it.” And concerning a man who entered upon another man who had a carpet with an image on it, he said: “Do not sit on it, and do not perform salat (prayer) on it.” Thus, the correct understanding of this report is that it indicates a degree of reprehensibility, not prohibition.

key_terms.التَّمَاثِيلُ: images or figures depicted on the carpet
key_terms.الْبِسَاطُ: a carpet or mat used for sitting or standing
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: reprehensibility or disliked status in legal context

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) on a carpet that has images on it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on standing or performing salat (prayer) on a carpet containing images. The wording indicates karāhah, meaning disapproval or reprehensibility, rather than outright prohibition, and reflects juristic guidance on prayer etiquette and the use of decorated furnishings.
